products.name: Ragas
products.note: Open-source RAG evaluation framework; defined the standard metric set (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, context recall); reference-free LLM-as-judge scoring

reading.body:
Exploding Gradients built Ragas, an open-source framework that standardized how to measure whether retrieval-augmented generation systems work, using LLM-as-judge scoring without ground-truth labels.

RAG evaluation matters because RAG is a primary path for adding real-world data to LLMs without retraining. Measuring whether a RAG pipeline retrieves the right context and produces faithful answers is necessary before deploying it. Ragas codified the metrics—faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, context recall—that the industry now uses as common language. This reduces friction for teams building RAG systems.

The framework is reference-free, meaning it judges quality without requiring humans to annotate correct answers first. This lowers the operational cost of evaluation, which scales linearly with deployment volume. For AI teams operating at scale, this removes a manual bottleneck.

The data does not cover Exploding Gradients' team size, governance structure, funding, or how Ragas revenue or adoption tracks. It does not measure how widely these metrics have been adopted beyond this single framework, or whether they have become industry standard or remain one option among several.

profile_text.body:
Exploding Gradients is an open-source software organization best known for developing Ragas, a framework for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines. The project is hosted on GitHub, and the harvested website text reflects GitHub's own platform description rather than a dedicated company site, so detailed information about the organization's founding, team, or structure is not available from the source material.

Ragas is categorized as an AI Governance and Risk Management platform and is described as having defined a standard metric set for RAG evaluation, covering faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall. It uses a reference-free, LLM-as-judge scoring approach, meaning evaluations do not require ground-truth annotations to produce scores. The framework is available at github.com/explodinggradients/ragas.

No litigation, SEC filings, patent records, or MCP server registrations are recorded in the held facts for Exploding Gradients.
